newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Santos stevedores begin indefinite strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Santos stevedores begin indefinite strike.

text.p: Stevedores at Brazil's Santos port began an indefinite strike at 0700 local time (1000 GMT), bringing to a halt the loading and unloading of ships at South America's largest port, a union official said.
The union official, who requested anonymity, said workers did not report to work today to protest a bill now before Congress that would strip them of 40 percent of their work.
"The stevedores are striking to defend their jobs," he said.
Port officials could not be reached to confirm the strike had begun or that it had paralyzed the port.
The union official said the stoppage comes as 25 ships are awaiting loading or unloading at Santos port and said that the strike could spread to the rest of Brazil's ports on Wednesday.
He also said that early in the morning federal police boarded two ships to oust protesting stevedores at steelmaker Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) facilities in Santos.
The workers have been protesting since April 2 over a company decision to hire a contractor to operate its Santos terminal privately. --James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 2485413
